thread:
maya: Heads-up — spotted a latency spike on the branch picker today :eyes: Looks like for SM89 the runtime picked FlashV3 causal path for head_dim=26 and seq_len ~1024 and latency doubled compared to previous baseline.
devon: Ugh. Is this in prod traffic or a perf test? Any profiling traces/artifacts?
maya: Prod, small percent of requests. Attached top-line from traces:
```
kernel_choice: flashv3_causal
device: sm_89
head_dim: 26
seq_len: 1024
batch: micro (1-4)
avg_token_ms: 12.8  # before ~6.1
kernel_ms_breakdown: flashv3_kernel=11.9, fallback_cpu=0.2, memcpy=0.7
```
raj: Do we have a perf counter or nvprof snippet? flashv3 shouldn't regress that much normally. Might be kernel selector misclassifying because head_dim isn't typical multiple of 8/16.
lina: Could be the tiling heuristics in v3 hitting a fallback kernel path that is slower on SM89 for non-standard head sizes. Remember earlier we saw odd behavior for head_dim=22 on SM90.
maya: I ran a quick `nvprof` on a repro VM. Snip: 
```
# nvprof summary
Time(%)  Time(ms)  Calls  Name
50.2%   6.2       320    flashv3_pack_qk_kernel
30.1%   3.7       320    flashv3_causal_compact
15.0%   1.8       640    memcopy
```
The pack kernel is super heavy. On SM80 the distribution is much more even.
devon: Can you paste the exact model config + request size? Also which kernelpicker rules matched? We should log the selector decision tree in the trace.
maya: Sure: model=redwood-7b-open, seqlen=1024, batch=3, head_dim=26, num_heads=32, quant=fp16, runtime flags: `branchpicker=v2, flash_pref=auto`.
perf-bot: Auto-analysis: similar spike detected in 7 other deploys across europe-3 region between 03:10-03:40 UTC. Affected p95 up by ~95% for kernels matching head_dim in [24,28].
raj: That pattern points to a binning issue in the kernelgraph. We bucket head sizes into groups [<=16,17-24,25-32] and possibly using wrong kernel for 25-32 for sm89. For v3 we have two internal tilings: T1 and T2. Maybe T2 was chosen but performs poorly on SM89 due to register pressure.
lina: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: add warmup hysteresis in the selector — require stable perf for N samples before switching to a more aggressive kernel. Also prefer architecture-specific overrides: e.g., for SM89 prefer T1 for head_dim in 25-28.
devon: Let's not hotfix in prod without tests. Proposed plan: 1) add detailed selector logging (which rule fired + cost estimate), 2) repro with microbench harness on SM89, 3) implement hysteresis with config flag `branchpicker.warmup_samples=12`, 4) canary rollout to 1%.
maya: I pushed a repro script to the perfbench repo: 
```
# repro command
./perfbench --model redwood-7b-open --device sm89 --seq 1024 --batch 3 --heads 32 --head-dim 26 --runs 500 --log kernel_choice,latency
```
devon: Running it now on a sm89 VM. If we confirm, I can add a quick guard in the selector: if device==sm89 && head_dim in [24..28] then prefer flashv2_causal until autotuner collects 100 samples.
raj: Collecting `cupti` traces as well. Also capture register utilization and shared memory stats — if register spilling is the culprit we'll see high local memory usage.
maya: One weirdness: the KV cache warmup appears correlated — cold streams (no KV warmup) hit the slow path more often. Maybe the autotuner uses warmup perf samples incorrectly when cache is empty.
lina: That suggests we should decouple autotune sampling from cold-cache runs. Add a flag `autotune.skip_cold_cache=true` so first N samples are excluded.
perf-bot: Observability note: created ticket PERF-3242 with pinned traces. Also added dashboard alert when branchpicker changes kernel for a route and p95 changes >20% within 30m.
devon: I'll open a PR with: enhanced logging, skip_cold_cache, and a config knob for warmup_samples. We'll gate the rollout behind `runtime.flags.branchpicker_canary`.
maya: Thanks. After the canary, if stable we'll backfill a binary-level override in the kernelgraph for SM89.
raj: Quick ask — add a small unit test in kernelpicker_test that enumerates head_dim 16..32 on SM89 emulator to ensure pick isn't oscillating.
lina: I'll own the canary rollout and metrics. If p95 stays within 10% of baseline for 24h we flip the flag.
maya: Great. I'll keep monitoring traces and post any new anomalies here. :rocket:
devon: Follow-ups: link PR, perfbench results, nvprof, and ticket number when available. Thanks all.
